resources.string: Stop everything and close Spatial Launcher?
Videos — pick and play on-device video
Playing video — tap reel again to stop
Open a video (reel) or cast an app so Listen can hear audio
No videos yet. Open one from Files to add it to this shelf.
Tap the reel → pick a video from Files. OCR / TTS / Share / 3D work on the picture; Listen hears the soundtrack (ear). 3D waits for a real frame before covering the player. Tap reel again to stop.
Opens the system picker for on-device video. Playing video uses the same OCR, TTS, Share, 3D, and Listen tools as cast/browser.
Tap a dock app → in the share sheet pick that app (Just this window). Leave 3D on (glasses). Tap power to stop.

Cast the show → OCR zones (sidebar) → box the subtitle band → Save → Done. Settings → Reader pipeline Read → Translate engine ML Kit OCR → TTS on → continuous (blue loop). Numbers on boxes are read order — add top first.
3. Listen when there are no subs

Cast an app or play a local video (reel), then tap the ear (turns red). Allow audio capture if asked (Android calls it Microphone — the mic itself is never used). First use downloads speech models (~1 GB) over Wi‑Fi — allow it when prompted. Translate uses bundled OPUS (JA/ZH/KO in the APK). Best with pause breaks between lines. Tap ear again to stop.
OCR zones on the text → Settings → Reader pipeline Translate → Translate engine OPUS → TTS on if you want it spoken.
Globe → open a page → Translate (on-device) or Google Translate (needs network). Turn TTS on, then Read, to hear it.
Tap book = My Books shelf (tap again or Close to dismiss). Tap a title to open it. Tap book again while reading to close. Long-press book = PC import on/off.

Install Spatial Launcher Desktop on Windows, Start Session, same Wi‑Fi. On Quest tap the monitor toolbar button — it auto-finds the PC. In Desktop Link: Headset 3D on for Horizon SBS; Live 3D / Full SBS / JPEG·MPEG·AV1 / Gaming·Movies and the sliders push to the PC while you stream. Point at the picture to show controls again after Min. PC sound/firewall details are in the Desktop docs — not needed on the headset.
Core cast / OCR / TTS work offline from the APK. Listen needs the one-time speech download below; only the items listed need Wi‑Fi when you use them.
Speech recognition (SenseVoice, ~1 GB) downloads once over Wi‑Fi — allow it when prompted. Translate then uses bundled OPUS JA/ZH/KO→EN. No Play Store needed.
Female and male Piper voices are both in the APK. Pick Male in Settings — unpacks locally, no download.
Japanese, Chinese, and Korean→English OPUS packs ship in the APK (same for store and desktop installer builds).
Needs network each time you use it — not a one-time offline pack. On-device page Translate does not need that download.
Female + male TTS, OPUS JA/ZH/KO, 3D depth, ML Kit OCR AARs — unpack from the APK locally.
Tap to toggle. Glasses = stereo depth on. Plain “3D” = flat. Listen turns 3D off while it runs.

Turn TTS on in Settings first (dim speaker = TTS off). Long-press the speaker to switch modes. Green speaker = tap to read once. Blue loop = keeps reading as OCR updates. Manual mode also shows prev/play/pause/stop/next.
Tap ear to start (red). Auto-turns TTS continuous + Assist Listen + 3D off. Tap again to leave Listen and turn TTS off.
Tap opens My Books; tap again closes the shelf. While a book is open, tap book again to close the reader. Long-press starts or stops PC EPUB import over Wi‑Fi.
Tap a pinned app to launch and cast it. Long-press asks to remove it from the dock.

Read = OCR→Piper (English). Translate/Share = OCR→OPUS→Piper when engine is OPUS. Share adds a caption overlay. Listen = audio→STT→OPUS→Piper. ML Kit OCR engine skips OPUS (as-read). Active: line shows the path; selected buttons are green.
Live updates depth as the picture moves. Static holds a steadier depth look (good for stills / less motion). Separate slider profiles per mode.
Ends the mirrored app window and returns to the dock.
Stereo depth toggle. See Dual-mode icons above.
Opens the built-in Widevine browser for streaming sites and web pages.
Library + PC import. See Dual-mode icons above.
Speaks OCR / page text. Once vs continuous via long-press. See Dual-mode icons above.
Cast audio → translate → speak. Red when on. Best with pause breaks. See Dual-mode icons above.

Opens a side panel to draw boxes over subtitles or dialogue so TTS / Translate read only those areas. With no boxes, only the lower cast dialogue band is read (not the whole app HUD). The number on each box is read order (add top first). Save per app.
Depth, TTS voice/speed, Reader pipeline, Translate engine (OPUS / ML Kit OCR), OCR / Listen smoothness, and other options.
On-device page translate line-by-line; can speak as it goes if TTS is on.
Uses Google’s page translate when you have network, then can polish / read.
Speaks the current page with Piper when TTS is enabled.
Mirror an app from the dock, then leave 3D on for a spatial view of that window.
English game — Read + ML Kit OCR
Reader pipeline Read, Translate engine ML Kit OCR, OCR zones, TTS continuous. OCR→Piper, no OPUS.
Reader pipeline Translate, Translate engine OPUS, OCR boxes on foreign text, TTS on. OCR→OPUS→Piper.
Reader pipeline Share. OPUS for foreign text or ML Kit OCR for English as-read. Shows caption on panel; speaks if TTS continuous is on.
Cast the app, tap the ear. No subs needed — it listens to audio. Prefer scenes with natural pauses. Use Settings → Listen smoothness if speech lags or feels choppy.
Open a page, tap Translate for offline/on-device, or Google Translate when online. Pair with TTS to hear it.

My Books → Import over Wi‑Fi (or long-press the book icon) to start PC import, then send an EPUB from Novel Translator on the same Wi‑Fi. Send fails? Import mode must be on, both on the same Wi‑Fi, and Novel Translator must Find headset again — the Quest IP changes and stale addresses refuse.
Listen = talk / no subs (audio). OCR + TTS / Translate = on-screen text / subs. Don’t run both for the same job.
3D off while the page translates. It comes back when the job finishes.
Page Translate reads line-by-line: translate → Piper speak → next. Page switches to English when finished.
My Books. Tap again to close shelf or open book. Long-press toggles PC import.
No books yet. Send an EPUB from Novel Translator, or open one from Files.

PC import is on

Desktop Novel Translator should find this automatically on the same Wi‑Fi.
Pick a mode. Active pipeline below always shows the path in use.
Active: OCR → Piper (ML Kit OCR · no OPUS)
Active: OCR → OPUS → Piper (foreign on-screen → English)
Active: OCR → Piper (Translate mode · OPUS off · ML Kit OCR)
Active: Audio → STT → OPUS → Piper (3D off)
Active: Audio → STT → Piper (Listen · OPUS off)
Active: OCR → OPUS → Piper + caption (share overlay)
Active: OCR → Piper + caption (Share · OPUS off · ML Kit OCR)
OPUS = machine translate for Translate / Share / Listen. ML Kit OCR = recognize and speak as-read (no OPUS; best for English).
Listen needs an app cast so it can hear that window
Listen captures the cast app’s audio — Android labels this “Microphone” permission, but your mic is never recorded
Listen stays off without audio-capture permission. Cast, OCR, Browser, and Books still work.
Needs Spatial Launcher Desktop on your Windows PC. Same Wi‑Fi → Start Session on PC → tap the monitor icon here.
Opens connected automatically from the monitor icon. Min hides this panel for 10s — then point your ray at the picture to show settings again.
Settings hidden for 10s — move your ray off the panel, then point at it again to show controls. Stream keeps playing.
Settings stay hidden a few more seconds — then point at the panel to show them.
Searching LAN for Spatial Launcher Desktop…
No PC found — open Spatial Launcher Desktop on the same Wi‑Fi (Link listens even before Start Session)
PC Link OK · waiting for Start Session frames
Horizon stereo API missing — showing flat SBS. Update Horizon OS if possible.
Point at the panel to show controls
PC not reachable on :8765 — open Spatial Launcher Desktop and Start Session, then Find PC
Halos around people: raise Edge smear clean, lower Motion ghosting
Listen on — TTS auto, 3D off. Cast an app to hear it.
Listen translate failed — will speak ASR text until OPUS is ready
Listen uses on-device speech recognition (~1 GB, one-time). Download now over Wi‑Fi? You can also do it later — Listen will ask again.
Connect to Wi‑Fi to download speech models (~1 GB)
Speech models still downloading — try again shortly
Listen needs its one-time speech download (~1 GB) — tap the ear icon
Higher = wait longer for a stable caption (fewer cuts/repeats). Lower = snappier, may speak partial lines.
Higher = longer phrases (smoother). Lower = smaller chunks (less lag behind video).
